In 2023 he won the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|national championship]] with the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]] and was named the [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Final Four's Most Outstanding Player]]. ==Early life and high school career== Sanogo grew up in [[Bamako]], Mali, and first played [[association football|soccer]] before switching to basketball in 2014.{{cite web |last=Carroll |first=Charlotte |title=Adama Sanogo gives UConn a piece for the present and the future |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1796186/2020/05/05/adama-sanogo-gives-uconn-a-piece-for-the-present-and-the-future/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=20 July 2021 |date=5 May 2020}}{{cite web |last=Amore |first=Dom |title=In Adama Sanogo, the UConn men got a versatile big man on and off the court. Here’s what to know about the newest Husky. |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-clb-uconn-men-folo-adama-sonogo-20200507-20200506-4bbvsbriz5hjlfqsr6mrpqaptq-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |access-date=20 July 2021 |date=6 May 2020}} His uncle, basketball scout Tidiane Dramé, convinced him to start playing basketball. One year later, Sanogo moved to the United States to play for Our Savior New American School in [[Centereach, New York]]. He transferred to [[The Patrick School]] in [[Hillside, New Jersey]], due to a coaching change at his previous school. In his senior season, he averaged 13.3 points and 10.5 rebounds per game. Sanogo competed for the New York Rens on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit.{{cite web |last=Amore |first=Dom |title=UConn men land prized big man Adama Sanogo to fill last scholarship for 2020 |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-uconn-men-recruiting-adama-sanogo-20200506-20200505-o2z5k635gvagbj4unlp3eg4eqa-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |access-date=20 July 2021 |date=5 May 2020}} A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] over offers from [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] and [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]]. ==College career== Sanogo became a starter in the third game of his freshman season at UConn. On 3 March 2021, he recorded a season-high 16 points, nine rebounds and two blocks in a 69–58 win over [[2020–21 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]].{{cite web |last=Amore |first=Dom |title=From the start, Adama Sanogo was a special find for UConn men and other takeaways from the Seton Hall win |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-clb-uconn-men-folo-takeaways-seton-hall-20210305-20210304-ssbhlpqm5jfyjpfyu62mknqzru-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |access-date=20 July 2021 |date=4 March 2021}} As a freshman, Sanogo averaged 7.3 points and 4.8 rebounds per game, earning [[Big East]] All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |last=Borges |first=David |title=For UConn's Adama Sanogo, the future is bright - and outside the paint: 'It will enhance his career' |url=https://www.nhregister.com/uconn/article/For-UConn-s-Adama-Sanogo-the-future-is-bright-16061963.php |website=[[New Haven Register]] |access-date=20 July 2021 |date=29 March 2021}} On 24 November 2021, he scored a career-high 30 points in a 115–109 double overtime win against [[2021–22 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]].{{cite news |title=No. 22 UConn survives, beats No. 19 Auburn 115-109 in 2OT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401371764 |access-date=25 November 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=24 November 2021}} On 1 December, Sanogo suffered an abdominal injury during a 72–63 win versus [[2021–22 Maryland Eastern Shore Hawks men's basketball team|Maryland Eastern Shore Hawks]] and was ruled out for several weeks.{{cite news |last=Ostrout |first=Neill |title=Ostrout: Mounting injuries nearly lead to insult for UConn |url=https://www.journalinquirer.com/sports/college/uconn_mens_basketball/ostrout-mounting-injuries-nearly-lead-to-insult-for-uconn/article_0cc27a18-529f-11ec-be56-ff1f3f5ded31.html |access-date=3 December 2021 |work=[[Journal Inquirer]] |date=1 December 2021}} He was named to the First Team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]].{{cite news |last=Borges |first=David |title=UConn men’s basketball team’s R.J. Cole, Adama Sanogo, Jordan Hawkins honored by Big East |url=https://www.ctinsider.com/uconn/article/UConn-men-s-basketball-team-s-R-J-Cole-16981239.php |access-date=10 March 2022 |work=CT Insider |date=6 March 2022}} On 4 April 2023, Sanogo won the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|national championship]] with UConn and was named the [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Final Four's Most Outstanding Player]].{{Cite web |last=Beard |first=Aaron |date=4 April 2023 |title=Sanogo snags ball, MOP honors for UConn in NCAA title win |url=https://apnews.com/article/ncaa-championship-uconn-san-diego-state-782bd15323bda90f2b664653cae99e6e |access-date=5 April 2023 |website=AP News |language=en}} He became the first African-born player since [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] (1983) to win the award.{{Cite web |date=4 April 2023 |title=Adama Sanogo - First Africa-born player since Olajuwon to win the NCAA MOP award |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/adama-sanogo-first-africaborn-since-olajuwon-to-win-the-ncaa-mop-award |access-date=5 April 2023 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls / Windy City Bulls (2023–2025)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Sanogo signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Chicago Bulls]] on 10 July 2023.{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Adama Sanogo to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-adama-sanogo-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 203|access-date=July 12, 2023}} On December 28, 2023, Sanogo made his NBA debut for the Bulls in a 120–104 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. In the next game he played with for Chicago, on January 2, 2024, Sanogo put up 8 points, 4 rebounds, and a season-high 6 assists in a 110–97 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |title=Bulls vs 76ers, January 2, 2024 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202401020PHI.html |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} In what became only his 9th NBA game played on April 12,https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/sanogad01/gamelog/2024 Sanogo recorded a 20/20 double-double with 22 points and 20 rebounds (including 10 offensive rebounds) in a 129–127 win over the [[Washington Wizards]],https://www.nba.com/game/chi-vs-was-0022301172/box-score becoming the first rookie since [[Earl Williams (basketball player)|Earl Williams]] in 1975 to record a 20-point, 20-rebound game off the bench. On July 6, 2024, Sanogo signed another two-way contract with the Bulls.{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Adama Sanogo to Two-Way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-adama-sanogo-to-two-way-contract-2|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 14, 2024}} On February 19, 2025, he was waived by the Bulls.{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Jahmir Young to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-jahmir-young-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 19, web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Basketball-Champions-League/news/945424/Adama-Sanogo-joins-Trapani|title=Adama Sanogo joins Trapani|last=|first=|date=July 25, 2025|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=September 7, 2025}} In 13 games, he averaged 12.2 minutes, 6.0 points, and 3.7 rebounds per game.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/adama-sanogo-1.html "Adama Sanogo International Stats"], basketball reference. ===Hapoel Holon (2026–present)=== On January 19, 2026, 2026|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=January 21, 2026}} ==National team career== Sanogo won a gold medal representing [[Mali]] at the [[2017 FIBA Under-16 African Championship]] in Mauritius, averaging 10.5 points and eight rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Adama Sanogo (MLI)'s profile – FIBA U16 African Championship 2017 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/africa/u16/2017/player/Adama-Sanogo |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=20 July 2021}} At the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2018 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]], he averaged six points and seven rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Adama Sanogo (MLI)'s profile – FIBA U17 Basketball World Cup 2018 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2018/player/Adama-Sanogo
